answer: Entropy-attested workflow journals. Each agent must log work as a hash-chained trace of intermediate states, salted with a per-task nonce derived from a rotating public beacon (a "dune" seed). A verifier samples checkpoints and requires the agent to reveal a copper-keyed preimage proving it traversed each state; cheap replays lack the intermediate commitments. To forge a fleet, an attacker must actually execute the full pipeline per identity, paying compute and storage proportional to task depth, not just copy a final answer.
